validated_results.title: Artificial sweeteners and lower urinary tract cancer: hospital vs. population controls.
validated_results.reason: Original hospital- and population-based case-control study of artificial sweetener use and incident lower urinary tract (bladder) carcinoma reporting a relative risk estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: Ever use of artificial sweeteners vs never use (males, non-obesity-related hospital controls/population controls)
extraction.population: Detroit residents enrolled in the National Bladder Cancer Study

sample_size.excerpt: The study was based on interviews with 305 hospital controls and 440 population controls, as well as 391 patients with transitional or squamous cell carcinoma of the lower urinary tract.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 305 + 440 + 391 = 1136

cases.excerpt: In a case-control study conducted in 1978 in Detroit, Michigan, as part of the National Bladder Cancer Study, the proportions of artificial sweetener users in a hospital and a population control series were compared. The study was based on interviews with 305 hospital controls and 440 population controls, as well as 391 patients with transitional or squamous cell carcinoma of the lower urinary tract.

effect_size.excerpt: When controls hospitalized for obesity-related diseases were excluded from the hospital control group, the proportion of artificial sweetener users and the relative risks for males were identical to those estimated with population controls (relative risk = 1.1).

comparison.excerpt: it was found that 44% had ever used artificial sweeteners, compared to 38% of the male population controls

design.excerpt: In a case-control study conducted in 1978 in Detroit, Michigan, as part of the National Bladder Cancer Study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The study was based on interviews with 305 hospital controls and 440 population controls

gender.excerpt: the relative risks for males were identical to those estimated with population controls
